title: Nvidia Open-Sources Flora Weights to Cut Robot Data Costs 125x
summary:
Researchers Jim Fan and Yunze developed a data engine that assigns timestamped instructions and reward signals to raw video footage of humans and robots. This suite of models, called Flora, is now open-sourced by Nvidia and delivers performance comparable to Astra at 125x lower cost. The system currently processes 200,000 hours of video daily using 500 GPUs to curate training signals for machine learning.

Nvidia employs Flora to train its GR00T robotics project, using dense progress rewards for reinforcement learning post-training and rubric scoring for real-world benchmarks. By releasing the weights to the public, the company aims to help developers scale the frontier of robot learning through the automated filtering of egocentric and robot data.

selectedTweets.text:
We built a robotics data engine with Astra-level performance at 125x lower cost. And we are open-sourcing the weights today! Introducing Flora, a suite of open models to parse the physical world and turn raw footage into rich training signals. 

Flora already powers our in-house data engine, labeling 200K hours of videos a day on 500 GPUs. We created it to scale the frontier for robot learning. Now you own the weights too. 

Flora gives you:

- High-quality, timestamped captions to curate and filter human egocentric and robot data;
- Dense progress rewards for quality control and RL post-training;
- Rubrics scoring for real-world benchmarking
